scribe.hint.newText: Start a new, empty text in a tab of its own. It has no file until you save it.
scribe.hint.open: Open one or several text files, each in its tab. The encoding and the line endings of each file are found and kept.
scribe.hint.save: Write the text to its file, in the encoding and with the line endings shown under the text.
scribe.hint.saveAs: Write the text to a new file; the old file stays as it was.
scribe.hint.reopen: For a file whose letters came out wrong: read its bytes again as another encoding. The file itself is not changed.
scribe.hint.close: Close this tab. You are asked first when the text has changes that are not saved.
scribe.hint.settings: The settings of Scribe: the letters of the editor, wrapping, line numbers.
scribe.hint.undo: Take back the last change, step by step. A tool applied to the text is one step.
scribe.hint.redo: Do again what was just undone.
scribe.hint.find: Find a word or a pattern in the text and, if you want, put something else in its place: one at a time or everywhere.
scribe.hint.wrap: Fold lines that are longer than the window, so nothing has to be scrolled sideways. The text itself is not changed.
scribe.hint.lineNumbers: Show the number of each line beside the text.
scribe.file.exported: Written as {name}. The text keeps its own file; the copy is for others.
scribe.problem.cannotOpen: The file could not be opened.
scribe.problem.cannotSave: The file could not be saved. It may be open in another program, or the folder cannot be written to.
scribe.problem.notText: This file is not text (it may be a picture, a program or a document of another kind).
scribe.problem.unknownEncoding: The program does not know this encoding.
scribe.problem.cannotEncode: The text has letters this encoding cannot write (the first is "{letter}"). Nothing was saved. Choose another encoding under the text (UTF-8 writes every letter) and save again.
scribe.problem.damaged: Some of the file is not text in {encoding}; those places show as �. Try "Read again in another encoding" (File menu) before changing anything.
scribe.notice.mixedEndings: The lines of this file end in different ways. Saving gives them all the ending shown under the text.
scribe.reopen.lead: The encoding of an old file can only be guessed. If the letters look wrong, choose the encoding the file was written in; its bytes are read again, and the file itself is not touched.
scribe.reopen.losesChanges: The changes you made since the file was opened will be lost.
scribe.status.selected: {count, plural, one {# character selected} other {# characters selected}}
scribe.status.encodingHint: The encoding the text is saved in. Changing it does not change the text; it counts at the next save.
scribe.status.lineEndingHint: How each line ends in the file. Windows programs expect CRLF; Linux and macOS use LF.
scribe.hint.toolsPanel: Shows or hides the tools beside the text.
scribe.tools.onAll: Applied to the whole text. Select a part to work on that part only.
scribe.tools.onSelection: {count, plural, one {Applied to the selection (# character).} other {Applied to the selection (# characters).}}
scribe.tools.matches: {count, plural, =0 {Found nowhere.} one {Found in # place.} other {Found in # places.}}
scribe.tools.nothingChanged: Nothing to change: the text is already so.
scribe.tools.changed.lines: {count, plural, one {# line changed.} other {# lines changed.}} Undo takes it back.
scribe.tools.changed.places: {count, plural, one {Changed in # place.} other {Changed in # places.}} Undo takes it back.
scribe.tools.badPattern: The pattern is not a valid regular expression:
scribe.tools.failed: The tool could not be applied.
scribe.tool.repairRomanian: Repair Romanian letters (ş → ș, ţ → ț)
scribe.toolHint.replace: Puts something else in place of every match, in one step. With a regular expression, $1 stands for the first group and \n for a new line. No pattern can freeze the program.
scribe.toolHint.sortLines: Puts the lines in order, by the rules of the program's language: each language has its own order of letters. For a text in another language, choose it under More choices: titles lose that language's articles too.
scribe.toolHint.reverseLines: The last line becomes the first.
scribe.toolHint.shuffleLines: Puts the lines in a random order; another one each time.
scribe.toolHint.numberLines: Writes its number before each line. In what stands between the number and the line, \t stands for a tab.
scribe.toolHint.emptyLines: Takes empty lines out, or leaves one where there were several.
scribe.toolHint.joinLines: Makes one line of all, with what you write between them (\t for a tab; nothing, to stick them together).
scribe.toolHint.splitLines: Starts a new line wherever what you write is found (\t for a tab). What you write is taken out.
scribe.toolHint.changeCase: Capitals and small letters, for sentences, titles or the names programmers write.
scribe.toolHint.cleanSpaces: Several spaces become one; spaces at the ends of lines go. Line breaks stay.
scribe.toolHint.trimLines: Takes the spaces and tabs off the ends of every line.
scribe.toolHint.quotes: Gives the text the quotation marks of a language, or the straight ones keyboards type. An apostrophe inside a word stays an apostrophe.
scribe.toolHint.removeDiacritics: ă → a, é → e, ß → ss: for file names, web addresses and systems that do not take other letters. Letters of other alphabets are left alone.
scribe.toolHint.repairRomanian: Old systems wrote Romanian with a cedilla under s and t. This puts the right letters, with a comma, so that a search typed on a Romanian keyboard finds the words.
scribe.toolHint.tabsToSpaces: Each tab becomes spaces up to the next stop, so the text looks the same.
scribe.toolHint.spacesToTabs: The spaces a line starts with become tabs. Spaces inside the line are part of the text and stay.
scribe.toolHint.stripHtml:
For the source of a web page (HTML) pasted here: the tags, scripts and styles go, and what a reader would see stays. "

Good day

" becomes "Good day". A text without tags is left as it is. To bring a page from its address instead, use the tool right under this one.
scribe.field.keepCase: Keep the capitals of what is replaced
scribe.field.keep: Of lines that are the same, keep
scribe.field.ignoreSpaces: Spaces around a line do not count
scribe.field.adjacentOnly: Only when they follow each other
scribe.field.separator: Between the number and the line
scribe.field.pad: Zeros in front, so numbers line up (01, 02…)
scribe.option.by.natural: Letters, numbers as numbers (file2 before file10)
scribe.option.by.numeric: The number each line starts with
scribe.option.mode.collapse: Leave one where there are several
scribe.option.to.title: Every Word A Capital
scribe.hint.stats: Shows or hides what the text is made of, beside it: words, sentences, time, the words used most.
scribe.stats.ofAll: Of the whole text. Select a part to count that part only.
scribe.stats.long: The text is very long: it is counted when you ask.
scribe.stats.topWordsNote: Words of fewer than four letters are left out: they are the small words of every language.
scribe.stats.topPairs: Pairs of words that come back
scribe.hint.compareWithFile: Compare this text, as it is now, with a file you choose: the lines only one of them has and, inside changed lines, the words that differ.
scribe.hint.compareFiles: Open a tab that shows two files side by side with what differs between them. The files are only read.
scribe.compare.title: Compare
scribe.compare.chooseBoth: Choose the two files to compare.
scribe.compare.failed: The texts could not be compared.
scribe.compare.identical: {count, plural, one {The two texts are the same (# line).} other {The two texts are the same (# lines).}}
scribe.compare.skipped: {count, plural, one {# line that is the same} other {# lines that are the same}}
scribe.hint.findInFolder: Look for a word or a pattern in every text file of a folder and of those under it, and, if you want, replace it there: every match is shown first, and only the files you leave ticked are written.
scribe.folder.title: Find in a folder
scribe.folder.lead: Choose a folder and what to look for. Finding only reads the files; nothing is written until you ask to replace.
scribe.folder.everything: Also hidden folders and those programs fill (.git, node_modules…)
scribe.folder.cannotRead: The folder could not be read.
scribe.folder.failed: The search could not be done.
scribe.folder.nothing: {searched, plural, one {Found nowhere (# file looked in).} other {Found nowhere (# files looked in).}}
scribe.folder.found: {places, plural, one {# place} other {# places}} in {files, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}, of {searched} looked in.
scribe.folder.skipped: {count, plural, one {# file passed over (not text, or too large).} other {# files passed over (not text, or too large).}}
scribe.folder.stopped: The search stopped at the most it gathers; there may be more.
scribe.folder.more: {count, plural, one {…and # more in this file.} other {…and # more in this file.}}
scribe.folder.replace: {files, plural, one {Replace in # file…} other {Replace in # files…}}
scribe.folder.confirm: {files, plural, one {# file will be written} other {# files will be written}}, {places, plural, one {# place changed} other {# places changed}}. This cannot be undone here.
scribe.folder.written: {files, plural, =0 {No file was written.} one {# file written} other {# files written}}{places, plural, =0 {} one {, # place changed.} other {, # places changed.}}
scribe.folder.problem.cannot-encode: its encoding cannot write the new text; left as it was
scribe.folder.problem.cannot-save: could not be written; left as it was
scribe.hint.recipes: Shows or hides the recipes beside the text: the tools you applied, kept under a name to run again.
scribe.recipes.none: No recipes yet. Apply some tools to a text and come back here to keep them under a name, or make a recipe from nothing with "New recipe".
scribe.recipes.applied: {count, plural, one {Done to this text: # tool} other {Done to this text: # tools}}
scribe.recipes.name: Name of the recipe
scribe.recipes.nameHint: For example: Clean a list of names
scribe.recipes.files: {count, plural, one {# file chosen.} other {# files chosen.}}
scribe.recipes.toFolder: Write the results into a folder (the files stay as they are)
scribe.recipes.inPlaceNote: The files are changed where they are. This cannot be undone here: keep a copy if they matter.
scribe.recipes.runOnFiles: {count, plural, one {Run on # file} other {Run on # files}}
scribe.recipes.ranOnText: Done. Undo takes the whole recipe back in one step.
scribe.recipes.ranOnFiles: {written, plural, =0 {No file written} one {# file written} other {# files written}}{untouched, plural, =0 {.} one {; # needed no change.} other {; # needed no change.}}
scribe.recipes.problem.cannot-encode: its encoding cannot write the result; not written
scribe.recipes.problem.destination-exist: a file of this name is already in the folder; it was left as it is
scribe.toolHint.fillerText: Writes text that means nothing, to see how a page looks when it is full: paragraphs, lists, headings or a whole page, as plain text, Markdown, HTML or JSON. It goes where the cursor is, in place of the selection.
scribe.toolHint.randomText: Writes passwords, letters, digits or identifiers picked at random, on this computer only. They go where the cursor is, in place of the selection.
scribe.field.classicStart: Start with “Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet” (Latin only)
scribe.field.noLookalikes: Leave out characters easily confused (0 O 1 l I)
scribe.tools.made: Written where the cursor was. Undo takes it back.
scribe.tools.tooMuch: That is more than can be written at once. Ask for less.
scribe.toolHint.restoreRomanian: Romanian typed without ă, â, î, ș, ț is written with them again. Words Scribe knows are changed; words that can be read in more than one way (fata, fată, față) are listed for you to choose. Words it does not know stay as they are.
scribe.field.guess: Choose the likelier form by itself where a word is doubtful
scribe.doubts.lead: {count, plural, one {# word can be written in more than one way. Choose:} other {# words can be written in more than one way. Choose for each:}}
scribe.doubts.more: {count, plural, one {…and # more. Settle these, then apply the tool again.} other {…and # more. Settle these, then apply the tool again.}}
scribe.doubts.stale: The text was changed since. Apply the tool again to see the words where they are now.
scribe.settings.editorNote: How a text looks while you work on it. Nothing here changes the text or its file.
scribe.settings.font.about.mono: Every letter takes the same room, as on a typewriter: columns and lists line up.
scribe.settings.font.about.sans: The letters of the rest of the program: easier to read in long passages.
scribe.settings.wrapHint: A line longer than the window goes on below instead of running out of sight. The text itself keeps its lines.
scribe.settings.lineNumbersHint: Each line has its number beside it.
scribe.settings.sample: Țară, față, înțelepciune — 0O 1lI — the quick brown fox
scribe.settings.newTextNote: What a new text is saved as. A file you open keeps what it has; both can be changed for one text on the line under it.
scribe.settings.newLineEnding.about.syst: Windows ends lines one way, Linux and macOS another. Programs on this computer expect its own.
scribe.settings.newLineEnding.about.crlf: For files that go to Windows, whatever this computer is.
scribe.settings.newLineEnding.about.lf: For files that go to Linux, macOS, or the web, whatever this computer is.
scribe.settings.newMark: Start the file with a byte order mark
scribe.settings.newMarkHint: Three bytes at the start that tell some older Windows programs the file is UTF-8. Most programs need none, and a few are confused by it.
scribe.settings.shortcutsNote: The keys of Scribe's commands, the same as in other editors.
scribe.settings.resetAllNote: Puts every setting of Scribe back as the program ships it. Your texts and your recipes stay.
scribe.recipes.nameTaken: Another recipe has this name. Choose another.
scribe.recipes.noSteps: No steps yet. Add tools from the list below, in the order they should run.
scribe.recipes.noChoices: This tool has nothing to choose.
scribe.recipes.stepNotReady: This step is missing a choice it cannot run without.
scribe.drop.hint: Drop the files here to open them as new texts
scribe.drop.skipped: {count, plural, one {# file could not be opened: it is not text, or it is larger than 64 MB (open such a file with File → Open).} other {# files could not be opened: they are not text, or are larger than 64 MB (open such files with File → Open).}}
scribe.recent.title: Opened lately
scribe.field.language: In the order of letters of
scribe.large.reading: Going through the file to find its lines…
scribe.large.notPaged: This file is too large for the editor and is written two bytes to a letter (UTF-16), so it cannot be shown a page at a time either. Save it as UTF-8 in the program that made it.
scribe.large.about: It is too large for the editor, so it is shown a page at a time, read from the file as you go. It can be searched and given to a recipe; it is not changed here.
scribe.large.recipe: Run a recipe on the whole file…
scribe.large.foundAll: {count, plural, one {Found in # place. Click it to go there.} other {Found in # places. Click one to go there.}}
scribe.large.foundSome: {count, plural, one {The first # place. There may be more further on.} other {The first # places. There may be more further on.}}
scribe.hint.preview: Shows what the open tool would give beside the text, with what differs marked, before you apply it.
scribe.settings.previewShownHint: While a tool is open, what it would give is shown beside the text, with the lines that differ marked. Nothing changes until you apply.
scribe.preview.title: Result
scribe.preview.openAsNew: Open the result as a new text
scribe.preview.compare: Compare the text with the result
scribe.preview.tooLong: The text is too long to show the result beforehand. Apply the tool: Undo takes it back.
scribe.preview.kind.same: Nothing would change: the text is already so.
scribe.preview.kind.reordered: The same lines, in another order.
scribe.preview.fact.removed: {count, plural, one {# taken out} other {# taken out}}
scribe.preview.removed: {count, plural, one {The line that would be taken out} other {The # lines that would be taken out}}
scribe.option.by.date: The date each line starts with
scribe.option.by.title: Titles (an article at the start does not count: The, A, An)
scribe.field.sortLines.order: The order, parted by commas (small, medium, large)
scribe.field.delimiter: Columns are parted by (\t for a tab)
scribe.field.keepHeader: The first line stays first (it names the columns)
scribe.field.blocks: Sort paragraphs, not lines (each by its first line)
scribe.field.trim: First take the spaces off the ends of lines
scribe.option.keep.none: None (only lines that are there once stay)
scribe.option.empty.collapse: One stays where there are several
scribe.field.skipStart: Characters at the start that do not count
scribe.field.skipEnd: Characters at the end that do not count
scribe.field.pattern: Compare only what this pattern finds (regular expression)
scribe.toolHint.countLines: Leaves each line once, with how many times it was there written before it. Empty lines are not counted.
scribe.option.order.asMet: As they come in the text
scribe.field.repeatedOnly: Only the lines that are there more than once
scribe.field.countLines.separator: Between the count and the line (\t for a tab)
scribe.toolHint.filterLines: Looks for something in every line and keeps only the lines that have it, or only those that do not.
scribe.field.filterLines.mode: The lines where it is found
scribe.stats.timeNote: At {reading} words a minute read, {speaking} said, {typing} typed and {handwriting} written by hand. The speeds are changed in Settings.
scribe.stats.topTriples: Groups of three words that come back
scribe.stats.nothingYet: Nothing comes back yet: the text is too short.
scribe.stats.easeNote: From 0 (very hard) to 100 (very easy), by the formula made for this language: it looks at how long the sentences and the words are, not at what they say.
scribe.stats.easeChoose: Choose the language the text is written in.
scribe.stats.easeNone: No formula is established for {language}; one made for another language would mislead. If the text is in one of the languages above, choose it.
scribe.stats.ease.plain: Plain: most adults read it with ease
scribe.stats.limit.title: Title of a page
scribe.stats.limit.caption: Caption
scribe.stats.limitsNote: In characters, spaces counted. The limits are the ones in common use; each place may change its own.
scribe.settings.pacesNote: The speeds the times in Statistics are reckoned with, and how many words make a page.
scribe.field.ownWords: The words, parted by spaces or commas
scribe.option.unit.page: Parts of a page (heading, paragraphs, list)
scribe.field.level: Level of the headings (1 is the largest)
scribe.field.limit: At most this many characters (0: no limit)
scribe.field.seed: Seed: the same number gives the same text (0: new every time)
scribe.toolHint.sampleData: Writes names, e-mail addresses, phone numbers, street addresses, dates or numbers put together at random, one to a line, or lines after a pattern of yours. The e-mail addresses end in example.com, where mail reaches no one; a phone number made at random may be someone's, so do not call it.
scribe.tools.matchFacts: {lines, plural, one {On # line} other {On # lines}}; {different, plural, one {all the same text.} other {# different texts.}}
scribe.tools.badPairs: A line is not a pair. Write each as: what to find => what to put in its place.
scribe.preview.notYet: The tool cannot run with these choices yet.
scribe.toolHint.replaceMany: Several find-and-replace pairs done in one step, from the first to the last; each works on what the one before left.
scribe.field.pairs: One pair to a line: find => replace with
scribe.toolHint.reverseText: Turns the letters or the words of every line around; each line stays in its place. To turn the order of the lines around, use "Reverse the order of lines".
scribe.option.reverseText.what.words: The order of the words (abc def → def abc)
scribe.option.reverseText.what.eachWord: The letters of each word (abc def → cba fed)
scribe.pane.pasteOver: Paste in place of the text (or of the selection)
scribe.pane.drag: Drag to give one side more room; double click to make them equal
scribe.pane.dragPanel: Drag to make the panel wider or narrower
scribe.preview.scrollTogether: Scroll the text and the result together
scribe.preview.stacked: Put the result under the text
scribe.preview.sideBySide: Put the result beside the text
scribe.compare.chooseOther: Choose the other text to compare the two.
scribe.start.title: What would you like to do?
scribe.start.lead: Choose one and paste or type your text; every other tool stays a click away, beside the text.
scribe.start.countAbout: Words, characters, sentences, reading time, the words used most.
scribe.start.replaceAbout: Everywhere at once, with patterns, seen before it is done.
scribe.start.duplicatesAbout: Lines that repeat, taken out; what goes is shown first.
scribe.start.compareAbout: What was added, taken out and changed, side by side.
scribe.start.sortAbout: By letters, numbers, dates, length, a column, or an order of yours.
scribe.start.reverseAbout: Letters, words, upside down, as in a mirror.
scribe.start.fillerAbout: Paragraphs, lists, headings; plain, Markdown, HTML or JSON.
scribe.start.drop: Files dropped on the window open too.
scribe.editor.empty: Type or paste the text here
scribe.hint.toolGroup: Shows or hides this group of tools in the panel. A tool chosen from a menu is shown all the same.
scribe.hint.compareWithText: Sets this text beside another one that you type or paste, and shows what differs.
scribe.hint.compareTexts: Opens a tab where two texts are typed or pasted side by side and compared.
scribe.compare.typeHere: Type or paste a text here
scribe.variant.changeCase.title: Every Word A Capital
scribe.variant.reverseText.words: Turn around: the order of the words
scribe.variant.reverseText.eachWord: Turn around: the letters of each word
scribe.tools.allHidden: Every group of tools is switched off. Switch one on in View → Tools shown, or choose a tool from the Format or the Tools menu.
scribe.preview.notApplied: Your text is on the left; nothing changes it until you apply a tool.
scribe.preview.hint.noTool: Open a tool, from the panel or from the menus: what it would do to your text is shown here before you apply it.
scribe.preview.hint.writes: This tool writes a text where the cursor is: it has no result to show beforehand.
scribe.preview.hint.choices: Fill in what the tool needs (what to find, for one) and the result is shown here.
scribe.preview.hint.empty: Type or paste a text on the left: the result of the tool is shown here.
scribe.preview.hint.same: Nothing to change: this tool would leave the text exactly as it is.
scribe.preview.applied: Applied. The text on the left is now the result.
scribe.compare.dragHeight: Drag to give the texts or the comparison more room; double click to put it back
scribe.tool.webPageText: Text of a web page (from its address)
scribe.toolHint.webPageText: Type the address of a page and its text is written where the cursor is: what a reader sees, without tags, scripts or styles. The program goes online for this, only now and only to that address; the page is fetched by the browser on this computer, without your cookies or sign-ins.
scribe.tools.webPage.not-an-address: This is not the address of a web page. Write it as in the browser: example.com/page.
scribe.tools.webPage.no-browser: No browser that can bring the page was found on this computer (Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome).
scribe.tools.webPage.failed: The page could not be brought: there may be no connection, the address may be wrong, or the page has no text.
scribe.compare.typeOther: Type or paste the other text too: the two are compared once both have something.
scribe.hint.toolPages: On: the panel shows the list of tools, then the tool you choose in its place, with a way back. Off: all the tools in one list, each opening where it stands.
scribe.tools.noToolFound: No tool has that in its name or in what it does.
